# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Pulses
A pulse increases a cairn's height by adding the stride plus a bonus based on the current height. The bonus equals how many complete stride-lengths fit into the current height (using integer division). Each new pulse recalculates this bonus from the updated height—you can't reuse previous calculations.

## Leaks
After a pulse completes, a leak removes marks based on the new height. You divide the post-pulse height by the leak size and lose one mark per complete chunk. Leaks only apply to heights reached after pulsing, never to the original height.

## Repeated Cycles with Drains
When combining pulses with a fixed drain, you repeat: pulse, then subtract the drain amount. The cairn gets taller if each pulse adds more than the drain takes away. Eventually, if the drain is large enough relative to pulse gains, the height drops to zero. The number of cycles needed isn't simply height÷drain because pulses add variable amounts.

## Origins (Working Backwards)
If you know a final height after multiple pulses, you can find the starting height by testing candidates. Work forward from each candidate through all the pulses to see which produces the target. There's always exactly one correct starting height.

## Merging Two Cairns
Merging combines two cairns using weighted shares (as decimals between 0 and 1). Apply each share to its respective cairn's height, floor the results, then add them. Next, find the shorter cairn and add a per-ten adjustment (shorter height ÷ 10, floored). Finally, apply the tether value by adding it to the result. The tether can be positive or negative.
